**Fail-open in brain-audit reverter-skip: window-base cancels live offender (D2 PR3)**

What: brain-audit.mjs reverter-skip (branch feat/issue-259-d2-pr3-net-parity-reverter-skip) fails OPEN — a live-at-HEAD ungoverned artifact gets [SKIP]-exempted and audit exits 0, violating the design's own A7 property.

Root cause: the loop applies netAddFull(sha) (FULL-WINDOW, direction-blind, no +1 base) to EVERY failing merge, including the offender itself. netAddFull's window is windowFrom^1..HEAD where windowFrom = oldest audited merge (merges[last]). If the offender's ORIGINAL add sits BEHIND the window base while a DELETE of it sits INSIDE the window, netAddFull counts the delete (-1) but not the balancing add, so the live re-add O nets 0 => exempt.

Concrete repro (verified empirically): main has ungoverned ADR adr-100-x.md (add A). Feature branch: merge R deletes it, merge O re-adds it (revert-of-a-revert, live at HEAD). Audit range A..HEAD => window merges {R,O}, A excluded. isResolvedAt(O,HEAD)={resolved:false} (directional netPresent correctly keeps O flagged) BUT netAddFull(O,from=R,to=HEAD)=0 => reverter-skip exempts adrPresence => "[SKIP] ... reverts offender (net-absent at HEAD)", exit 0. adr-100-x.md is LIVE and ungoverned at HEAD.

Where: brain/scripts/brain-audit.mjs:376 (netAddFull exemption applied to offender), :262-268 (windowFrom = merges[last]).

Why the A7 fixture (brain-audit.test.mjs) misses it: A7 builds base..HEAD with the original add O as the OLDEST audited merge (inside the window), so netAddFull(R2) counts O(+1)+R2(+1)-R(-1)=+1 and correctly reports. It never exercises "original add before window base, delete inside". All 21 tests pass while the real audit fails open.

Contrast: netPresent (directional (O,HEAD], used by resolved-skip) is IMMUNE because it never counts merges before O. The full-window netAddFull re-opens the hole resolved-skip closes. Design explicitly claims "a revert-of-a-revert that re-adds a payload stays flagged" — implementation contradicts this when the first add is behind the window base.

Secondary finding: the SIG mirror comment (brain-audit.mjs:111-120) claims coarser drift => EXTRA [FAIL-SHA]. That is BACKWARDS: coarser = more sig collisions = SUPPRESSED (missed) [FAIL-SHA] = fail-open for the auto-revert consumer. crossCheckExit compares booleans (>0) not counts, so partial suppression (treeKeyedFailCount=2, failShaCount=1) still returns exit 1, not 2 — the coherence guard cannot detect a partially-suppressed emission. Mirror is currently byte-identical to resolution.mjs normDiff so no live exploit, but the documented safety rationale used to justify not locking it is inverted.

Learned: directional (netPresent) vs full-window (netAddFull) net-parity are NOT interchangeable for an OFFENDER; only the reverter/cleanup commit should be tested with netAddFull. The audit-window base (origin/main) truncates the accounting.
